sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Primary Source Value**: Travelers provide non-indigenous perspectives on the **Nayankara system** (military feudalism) and the **Ayagar system** (village administration).
• **Economic Observations**: Detailed accounts of the **Hampi bazaar**, international trade in horses, and the prosperity of the **Vijayanagar capital**.
• **Social Documentation**: First-hand reports on the prevalence of **Sati**, the status of women, and the religious tolerance of the rulers.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The reliability of accounts varies based on the traveler's cultural bias, linguistic limitations, and proximity to the royal court.

items.definition: A military-feudal system where 'Nayakas' were granted land (Amaram) in exchange for maintaining troops and paying tribute to the King.
A village-level administrative mechanism involving 12 hereditary officials (Ayagars) who managed local resources and tax collection.

items.title: Major Applications
items.content:
• **Historical Reconstruction**: Used to verify epigraphic evidence (inscriptions) found in Hampi.
• **Economic Analysis**: Used to map the global trade routes connecting Vijayanagar to the Middle East and Europe via the Portuguese.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Eurocentric bias in Portuguese accounts; linguistic barriers leading to misinterpretation of local customs.
• **Solutions**: Cross-referencing foreign accounts with indigenous literary works like 'Rayavachakam' and 'Krishnaraya Vijayam'.

items.title: Mnemonic for Chronology
items.content:
• **Phrase**: 'I Need A Perfect New Friend'
• **Decoded**: **I**bn Battuta (14th C) -> **N**icolo de Conti -> **A**bdur Razzak -> **P**aes -> **N**uniz -> **F**rederick (16th C).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often swaps the rulers visited by Abdur Razzak and Nicolo de Conti. Remember: Razzak visited Devaraya II (the greatest Sangama ruler).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Cosmopolitan Urbanism' when describing the accounts of Abdur Razzak regarding the Hampi markets.

keyTakeaways: Foreign accounts are essential for understanding the non-political aspects of Vijayanagar, such as social customs and trade.
The Portuguese accounts (Paes/Nuniz) are the most detailed regarding the Tuluva dynasty, specifically Krishnadevaraya.
Always cross-reference traveler accounts with the specific dynasty ruling at that time to avoid chronological errors in MCQs.
